Sirius Max combines color and depth with programmable beam steering

Leopard Imaging and Lumotive introduced an RGB-D module for robotics, claiming depth sensing beyond 20 meters and one-megapixel depth resolution.

PR Newswire ↗24 September 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

An integrated perception module

Leopard Imaging and Lumotive introduced Sirius Max, combining RGB imaging, indirect time-of-flight depth sensing and processing for robots and automation. The module is intended to supply synchronized color and depth information in real time.

Software controls where light goes

Lumotive’s TX10 transmitter and LCM technology steer illumination toward software-selected regions. The developers describe a fully solid-state design without moving mechanical parts, allowing sensing priorities to change instead of relying on fixed flood illumination.

One connection for imaging and control

The module uses an onsemi AF0130 depth sensor and GMSL2 to carry synchronized RGB video, depth and control over a coaxial cable. Proposed uses include navigation, mapping, cliff detection, collision avoidance and object handling.

Performance remains a manufacturer claim

Lumotive reports iToF operation beyond 20 meters indoors and outdoors with one-megapixel depth resolution. The announcement does not provide independent benchmarks, pricing or a delivery date. Performance still needs assessment with the actual materials, lighting and motion of a deployment.
